Bill.BriefDescription: Authorizing fees to implement programs that protect and improve Washington's health, safety, employees, and consumers.

BillBody.BillTitle: AN ACT Relating to fees to implement programs that protect andimprove Washington's health, safety, education, employees, andconsumers; amending RCW 39.12.070, 43.22.434, 70.74.137, 70.74.140,70.74.142, 70.74.144, 70.74.146, 70.74.360, 15.58.070, 15.58.180,15.58.200, 15.58.205, 15.58.210, 15.58.220, 17.21.070, 17.21.110,17.21.122, 17.21.126, 17.21.129, 17.21.220, 18.240.050, 18.250.080,18.260.020, 18.74.030, 18.74.070, and 18.74.073; adding a new sectionto chapter 70.74 RCW; adding new sections to chapter 18.130 RCW; addinga new section to chapter 18.84 RCW; adding a new section to chapter16.36 RCW; adding a new section to chapter 18.185 RCW; adding a newsection to chapter 18.74 RCW; creating new sections; providingeffective dates; and declaring an emergency.
BillBody.EnactingClause: BE IT ENACTED BY THE LEGISLATURE OF THE STATE OF WASHINGTON:

BillSection.RCWSLText: To protect taxpayers, many state programsrequire the costs of licensing, registration, certification, andrelated government services to be borne by the profession or industrythat uses the services, rather than by the taxpaying public as a whole.State standards that govern the professional duties of these industriesare intended to protect the general public by safeguarding health, p. 1 SHB 3381safety, employees, and consumers. The legislative approval of thefees and fee increases in this act is intended to ensure that thegeneral public is not assessed these costs while also providingadequate funding to statutory programs that safeguard and improveWashington's health, safety, employees, and consumers.

BegSecAmd.BegSecText: RCW 39.12.070 and 2006 c 230 s 1 are each amended to readas follows:

BillSection.SectionCaption: DEPARTMENT OF LABOR AND INDUSTRIES-PREVAILING WAGE-CERTIFICATIONOF AFFIDAVITS.
BillSection.RCWSLText: The department of labor and industries may charge feesto awarding agencies on public works for the approval of statements ofintent to pay prevailing wages and the certification of affidavits ofwages paid. The department may also charge fees to persons ororganizations requesting the arbitration of disputes under RCW39.12.060. The amount of the fees shall be established by rulesadopted by the department under the procedures in the administrativeprocedure act, chapter 34.05 RCW. The fees shall apply to allapprovals, certifications, and arbitration requests made after theeffective date of the rules. All fees shall be deposited in the publicworks administration account. The department may refuse to arbitratefor contractors, subcontractors, persons, or organizations which havenot paid the proper fees. The department may, if necessary, requestthe attorney general to take legal action to collect delinquent fees. The department shall set the fees permitted by this section at alevel that generates revenue that is as near as practicable to theamount of the appropriation to administer this chapter, including, butnot limited to, the performance of adequate wage surveys, and toinvestigate and enforce all alleged violations of this chapter,including, but not limited to, incorrect statements of intent to payprevailing wage, incorrect certificates of affidavits of wages paid,and wage claims, as provided for in this chapter and chapters 49.48 and49.52 RCW. However, the fees charged for the approval of statements ofintent to pay prevailing wages and the certification of affidavits ofwages paid shall be ((no greater than twentyfive)) forty dollars.
Section 2 of this act takes effect July 1,2008.

BillSection.RCWSLText: (1) For the 2008-09 academic year, the state board forcommunity and technical colleges may increase tuition and fees by nomore than two percent over tuition and fees charged to resident andnonresident students for the 2007-08 academic year. For the 2007-2009biennium, the state board for community and technical colleges mayincrease tuition fees under this subsection differentially based onstudent credit hour load at their discretion, provided that the overallincrease in average tuition revenue per student does not exceed twopercent. (2) The state board for community and technical colleges mayincrease tuition and fees by no more than five percent over tuition andfees charged for upper division courses in applied baccalaureateprograms in the 2007-08 academic year. (3) For the 2008-09 academic year, the technical colleges mayincrease operating fees by no more than two percent over operating feescharged to full-time resident and nonresident students for the 2007-08 SHB 3381 p. 18 academic year, to conform with the percentage increase in communitycollege operating fees. (4) For the 2008-09 academic year, technical colleges may increasetheir building fee by three cents per clock hour and by forty-fivecents per credit hour. The purpose of these fee increases is toprogress towards parity with the community colleges. (5) The state board for community and technical colleges mayincrease the maximum allowable services and activities fee up to twopercent in the 2008-09 academic year. BegSecAmd.BegSecText: RCW 18.250.080 and 2007 c 253 s 9 are each amended toread as follows:

BillSection.RCWSLText: (1) Each applicant and license holder must comply withadministrative procedures, administrative requirements, and fees under SHB 3381 p. 24 RCW 43.70.250 and 43.70.280 and subsection (2) of this section. Thesecretary shall furnish a license to any person who applies and who hasqualified under the provisions of this chapter. (2) The secretary must collect fees under this chapter as follows: (a) Application fee, one hundred seventyfive dollars; (b) Renewal fee, two hundred dollars; (c) Late renewal penalty fee, two hundred dollars; (d) Expired license reactivation fee, one hundred dollars; (e) Inactive license reactivation fee, forty dollars; (f) Duplicate license copy fee, fifteen dollars; and (g) License verification fee, twentyfive dollars.

BegSecAmd.BegSecText: RCW 18.260.020 and 2007 c 269 s 2 are each amended toread as follows:

BillSection.RCWSLText: (1)(a) No person may practice or represent himself or herself as aregistered dental assistant by use of any title or description withoutbeing registered by the commission as having met the standardsestablished for registration under this chapter unless he or she isexempt under RCW 18.260.110. (b) The secretary must collect the following fees from personsseeking or maintaining the status of a registered dental assistantunder this chapter: (i) Application fee, forty dollars; and (ii) Renewal fee, twenty dollars. (2)(a) No person may practice or represent himself or herself as alicensed expanded function dental auxiliary by use of any title ordescription without being licensed by the commission under this chapterunless he or she is exempt under RCW 18.260.110. (b) The secretary must collect the following fees from personsseeking or maintaining the status of a licensed expanded functiondental auxiliary under this chapter: (i) Application fee, one hundred seventyfive dollars; and (ii) Renewal fee, one hundred sixty dollars.

BegSecAmd.BegSecText: RCW 18.74.030 and 2007 c 98 s 3 are each amended to readas follows:

BillSection.RCWSLText: (1) An applicant for a license as a physical therapist shall havethe following minimum qualifications: p. 25 SHB 3381 (a) Be of good moral character; and (b) Have obtained either (i) a baccalaureate degree in physicaltherapy from an institution of higher learning approved by the board or(ii) a baccalaureate degree from an institution of higher learning anda certificate or advanced degree from a school of physical therapyapproved by the board. (2) An applicant for a license as a physical therapist assistantmust have the following minimum qualifications: (a) Be of good moral character; ((and)) (b) Have successfully completed a boardapproved physical therapistassistant program; and (c) Pay a license application fee of one hundred dollars to thesecretary. (3) The applicant shall present proof of qualification to the boardin the manner and on the forms prescribed by the board.

BegSecAmd.BegSecText: RCW 18.74.070 and 2007 c 98 s 8 are each amended to readas follows:

BillSection.RCWSLText: (1) Every licensed physical therapist and physical therapistassistant shall apply to the secretary for a renewal of the license andpay ((to the state treasurer)) a fee determined by the secretary asprovided in RCW 43.70.250 and 43.70.280. (2) Every physical therapist assistant seeking to renew his or herlicense must pay a fee to the secretary as follows: (a) Renewal fee, one hundred twentyfive dollars; (b) Late renewal fee, sixtytwo dollars and fifty cents; and (c) Expired license reissuance fee, seventyfive dollars.

BegSecAmd.BegSecText: RCW 18.74.073 and 2007 c 98 s 9 are each amended to readas follows:

BillSection.RCWSLText: (1) Any physical therapist or physical therapist assistant licensedunder this chapter not practicing physical therapy or providingservices may place his or her license in an inactive status. The boardshall prescribe requirements for maintaining an inactive status andconverting from an inactive or active status. The secretary mayestablish fees for alterations in license status. (2) The secretary must collect the following fees from a physical SHB 3381 p. 26 therapist assistant seeking to place his or her license on inactivestatus: (a) Inactive status fee, fifty dollars; and (b) Expired inactive status reissuance fee, seventyfive dollars.

BegSecNew.BegSecText: A new section is added to chapter 18.74 RCWto read as follows:

BillSection.RCWSLText: The secretary must collect the following fees from physicaltherapist assistants under this chapter: (1) Issuance of a duplicate license fee, fifteen dollars; and (2) Certification of a license fee, twentyfive dollars.
